claims.statement: To a uniform non-identity P in G1 and uniform z in GT, return Q in G2 with e(P, Q) = z, reduce to a discrete logarithm in GT by one pairing against the public generator of the unknown side and return the scalar multiple of that generator, as specified in proof.md. The single-seed Floyd walk succeeds with probability at least 0.39 over the uniform challenge and fresh algorithm coins; z = 1 returns the point at infinity. Total classical work is at most W = 2395039763148592466895916532144209349628 target-group-operation equivalents (dense Fp12 multiplications plus other instructions divided by C = 20000). The declared score 130815246/1000000 = 130.815246 is a ceiling of log2(W). Peak memory is at most 2^20 bytes. Preprocessing independent of the challenge is at most 53688 reference units (log2 ceiling 15.712313) and is included in W. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success figure is the same disclosed lower bound as in proof.md, not a production inversion and not a number-field-sieve estimate.

experiments.purpose: Recompute W from the public order and the instruction constants, check that the declared rational is a 10^(-6) ceiling of log2(W), and recover scalars on three prime-order additive groups. This does not establish production mixing, memory, or cost.
